faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Quick answers about the map, live tracking, and modded Valheim.
faq.moreHelpDescription: Send us a message from the app.

thunderstore.question: How do I use live tracking with Thunderstore mods?
thunderstore.answer: Start Valheim once with Thunderstore's Start modded button while Valheim Map is open. The app adds the tracker to the active profile. Fully close Valheim, then choose Start modded again to begin tracking. Thunderstore can stay open. If the profile is not detected, choose its folder in Settings.

tracker.question: Do I need to install the tracker myself?
tracker.answer: Valheim Map installs its bundled tracker automatically. If Valheim was already running when it was installed or updated, restart the game once to load it.

world.question: How do I see my own world on the map?
world.answer: Choose a local or Steam Cloud world save in the world selector. You can also enter a seed to explore a world without selecting a save.

overlay.question: How do I open the map while playing?
overlay.answer: Press Ctrl+M by default. You can change the overlay hotkey or turn on automatic opening in Settings.

inventory.question: Where does my inventory data go?
inventory.answer: The tracker writes inventory data to files on your computer so the crafting planner can count what you own. You can turn inventory tracking off in Settings.

colours.title: Reading the colours
colours.caption: Blue touches the ground; green → red is support draining as you go up. Under the minimum (10 for wood) a piece is destroyed — the ninth pole is already gone.
colours.try: Hover each pole from the bottom up, then right-click a low pole.

materials.title: Wood, core wood, iron, stone
materials.caption: Same 2 m poles, four materials: wood tops out near 16 m, core wood 24 m, iron 48 m; stone starts high but drains as fast as wood.
materials.try: Stack more iron on top; then give the wood tower a core-wood pole lower down.

sideways.title: Reaching sideways
sideways.caption: Wood loses 20 % per metre sideways against 12.5 % going up, so beams hung off one post fade to red by the fifth.
sideways.try: Rebuild the run with core wood or iron beams and count how far each reaches.

bridge.title: Hold it from both ends
bridge.caption: A piece with supports on opposite sides averages them at the gentler vertical rate — the same four beams stay healthy between two posts.
bridge.try: Right-click the far post of the second span and watch the run recolour.

floors.title: Floors between walls
floors.caption: Floor between two walls shares its load with both sides; the same tiles past a wall drain tile by tile until they fall.
floors.try: Add a wall under the fading row and see the tiles beyond it recover.

stone.title: Stone only stands on stone
stone.caption: Stone gets nothing from the side (100 % horizontal loss): a wall touching only a neighbour's flank falls; anything on top of stone — or on an iron beam — holds.
stone.try: Move the falling wall onto the column, then stack stone along the iron beam.

rock.title: Build on rock
rock.caption: Anything that is not a build piece — ground, boulders, trees, ruins — hands out full support wherever it is: this beam at 5 m is as blue as a post in the dirt.
rock.try: Drop a floor on the rock, then run beams to the pole tower and see where they meet.

iron.title: Iron re-grounds wood
iron.caption: A piece borrows its neighbour's number, capped at its own maximum: wood on an iron pole holding 400 restarts at 100 even 16 m up; wood on a red wood pole gets 12.
iron.try: Hover the beams off both columns at the same height, then extend the iron side.

house.title: A wood house, four storeys
house.caption: Three wood storeys hold; the fourth is already yellow, because every panel passes on about 74 % of the one below.
house.try: Swap the corner posts for iron poles and watch every wall go blue.

reference.title: Structural integrity, by the numbers

ground.title: Ground, rocks, trees, ruins
ground.body: touching anything that is not a build piece (within 15 cm) grants full support at any height.

bridge.title: Two-sided support
bridge.body: support points more than 100° apart around a piece are averaged at the vertical loss rate.

stronger.title: Stronger neighbours
stronger.body: a piece takes its neighbour's number minus its own loss, then clamps to its own maximum — wood on iron, stone or grausten restarts at 100.

noSupport.title: Pieces that carry nothing
noSupport.body: Dvergr, hexagonal and ashwood doors, armour stands, food and mead displays, carts, ships and the marble spire pass no support and cannot be built on.

rain.title: Rain and wet
rain.body: unroofed plain wood, wood-iron and iron cage pieces lose 5 % health every 60 s while wet, down to 50 %; roofs, darkwood, stone, marble and grausten do not.

shelter.title: Shelter
shelter.body: 17 rays over 30 m — sheltered/Rested and beds need 80 % blocked plus a roof; roofed crafting stations need 70 %.

reference.source: Source: WearNTear, Cover and SE_Rested in assembly_valheim.dll and the prefab data in the game's asset bundles.
